title: Hazrat Ayyub (A.S.) – A Timeless Lesson in Patience and Faith

author: Nazia Firdous
contentHtml:
Introduction

Life is never free from trials. Yet among all stories of patience and steadfast faith, the story of Prophet Ayyub (A.S.) stands out as a shining example. His journey shows that even in the darkest moments, turning to Allah ﷻ with unwavering trust brings ultimate reward.

His Life Before the Test

Hazrat Ayyub (A.S.) was blessed with wealth, children and health. He was known for his generosity and constant gratitude to Allah. His life reminds us that blessings are a trust from Allah, not merely our own achievements.

Severe Trials from Allah ﷻ

Allah tested Ayyub (A.S.) by taking away his wealth, children and health. Despite losing everything, he remained patient and continued to remember Allah.

“Indeed, We found him patient, an excellent servant. Indeed, he was one repeatedly turning back to Allah.”

(Qur’an, Surah Sad 38:44) – Read the verses on Quran.com

Patience (Sabr) and Complete Trust (Tawakkul)

Even in illness and poverty, Ayyub (A.S.) never complained. His famous supplication was:

“Indeed, adversity has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful.” (Qur’an 21:83)

This short, humble dua shows how believers should turn to Allah during trials.

Allah’s Mercy and Reward

After years of suffering, Allah restored Ayyub’s health, doubled his wealth and blessed him again with children. His story proves that after hardship comes ease—but the true reward lies in a heart that remains steadfast.

Lessons for Us Today

Patience in Hardship: Trials are a sign of Allah’s love, not His anger.

Gratitude in Ease: Like Ayyub (A.S.), thank Allah during times of comfort.

Hope in Allah’s Mercy: No matter how long the trial lasts, Allah’s plan is always best.

Urdu Section – حضرت ایوب علیہ السلام سے صبر کا درس

حضرت ایوب علیہ السلام کی زندگی صبر و استقامت کی روشن مثال ہے۔ آپ کو دولت، صحت اور اولاد کی نعمتیں عطا تھیں مگر اللہ نے سخت آزمائش میں ڈالا۔ مال و اولاد چھن گئے، صحت جاتی رہی، مگر آپ نے شکوہ نہیں کیا بلکہ صبر کیا اور اللہ کو یاد کرتے رہے۔

قرآن مجید میں فرمایا گیا:

"ہم نے ایوب کو صابر پایا۔ وہ بہترین بندہ تھا جو بار بار اللہ کی طرف رجوع کرتا تھا۔" (ص: 44)

سالوں کی آزمائش کے بعد اللہ تعالیٰ نے صحت، مال اور اولاد سب کچھ لوٹا دیا۔ یہ واقعہ ہمیں سکھاتا ہے کہ صبر کا انجام ہمیشہ خیر اور اللہ کی رحمت ہوتی ہے۔

🌟 Call to Action

English: Think of a trial you are facing. Whisper a short dua like Prophet Ayyub (A.S.): “Adversity has touched me and You are the Most Merciful.”

اردو: اپنی زندگی کی کسی آزمائش کو یاد کریں اور ایوب علیہ السلام کی دعا دل سے پڑھیں: "انی مسنی الضر و انت ارحم الراحمین"۔
